source_note: Extracted from the attached RAKSHA360 audit report and project documentation; verify any value against the implementation before treating it as the current runtime value.

runtime_parameters.meaning: Server-side missing-heartbeat threshold before a DEVICE_OFFLINE incident may be created.
Retry backoff for failed/pending recipients; do not resend recipients already marked SENT.
Architecture report says Guard Mode periodic heartbeat is 60 seconds.
Architecture report says location stream uses a 5-second interval when active.
Speaker-embedding acceptance threshold reported by audit; calibrate in real device testing.
Voice trigger phrase from audit; no loudness-only trigger.
PIN expires 10 minutes after scheduled pickup time.
Lock/require review after repeated failed PIN attempts.
API model cap noted in the audit implementation.
REST fallback polling interval noted in the audit report.
WebSocket reconnect delay noted in the audit report.

safety_invariants: Powered-off phone cannot transmit new GPS; use only the last location previously received and display its timestamp as NOT LIVE.
A missed heartbeat does not prove the phone is switched off; it can reflect coverage loss, app/service shutdown, or laptop/backend downtime.
Only send last-known-location email after explicit user consent, active email contacts, and successfully configured SMTP.
Never claim SMTP accepted equals inbox delivery.
Dispatch entries are internal control-room records; official police/112 gateway is NOT_CONFIGURED unless an authorized integration is actually provisioned and verified.
Real public station contact records must be classified OFFICIAL_PUBLIC_DIRECTORY and never blended into synthetic unit performance metrics.
All synthetic SOS/report/device/dispatch fixture rows use is_demo=true and clear DEMO display labels.
Never use real victim identities, real phone numbers, real emergency contacts, actual personal case narratives or private police records in fixtures.
Coordinates outside geographic bounds or absent coordinates must not be rendered as map markers.
Never use annual NCRB aggregate counts as incident pins, real-time alerts, or deterministic predictions.
